description: Seed of the fastener-library stream (DRAFT_tolerance_stack_mvp groundwork item 1). Every entry here carries INLINE values transcribed from a stack workbook and/or an assembly parts list -- none of them come from a fastener standard document, because no NAS/MS standard PDF exists in this repo. `library_ref` is the slot a real library entry drops into; when it is filled, `values_status` moves from `inline` to `library` and the inline numbers become a cross-check rather than the source.

entries.library_ref_note: FILLED 2026-08-05 by handoff spec_library_v0 -- the first entry in this file to defer to the spec library, and the demonstration of the seam docs/tolerance_stacks/hardware_entries.json's own description promised: "when it is filled, values_status moves from inline to library and the inline numbers become a cross-check rather than the source". `dimensions_in` below is now exactly that cross-check: every one of its numbers is re-derivable from the library subject NAS6403U11D, and `test_the_nas6403_hardware_entry_defers_to_the_library` asserts each one against it. Nothing on the STACK side changed -- stack_pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.json's elements still cite the standard through their own source_ref, which is the zero-rework property the slice-1 lesson designed the slot for. Resolve the ref against data/projections/spec_library/library.json (rebuild: python -m tolerance_stack). The other twelve entries keep values_status "inline" and belong to sop_edits_apply's backfill.

values_source.note: FIRST entry in this file whose inline numbers come from the actual standard rather than from the 260729 workbook or a parts list. `hardware_entry/v0` has no field for citing where inline values came from, so `values_source` is an additive extension proposed by handoff pitch_link_stack -- see LESSONS_20260804_pitch_link_stack.md. Scan with no text layer; read by vision. Part-number decode from the sheet-2 CODE block: 'U' after the basic number = unplated, 'D' after the dash number = drilled shank, dash number = grip in .0625 increments.

assembly_status.note: The fastener the drawing selects at the 5-place pitch-link joint. Slice 1's tan-link worksheet already noted it as '38, a different 5x joint'.

gaps: The THREAD RUN-OUT / incomplete-thread length is still not sourced. NAS6403 dimensions grip (to the end of the full cylindrical shank) and length (to the point) and gives T = .323 in as a reference between them, but never dimensions the transition itself. So slice 1's 1/16 in 'thread transition allowance' remains an uncited rule of thumb; the document that would close it is MIL-S-8879 (the thread spec sheet 1 invokes for UNJF-3A), which is not in data/inbox/specs/.

Sheet 5 of 5 is MISSING from the PDF. Sheet 1's LIST OF CURRENT SHEETS names five sheets (1 rev 4, 2 rev 2, 3 NEW, 4 rev 2, 5 rev 3); the file holds four. Nothing this stack uses lives on sheet 5, but a library ingest must not assume the file is complete.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 (spec_library_v0): the MEANING of dimension M (.174/.154) is read off the sheet-1 figure's extension lines, not from any text -- the standard never defines M in words -- and was the highest-value item for a second reader to confirm. A second reader has now confirmed it, at Matrix(14) on the pt rect [340,108,400,185]: M's left extension line is the long vertical that runs down through the shank to the drilled cotter hole's centerline, and its right terminus is the point end face. So M IS cotter-hole centerline to point. Recorded on the library subject NAS6403U11D. The remaining figure-read value on this entry is `point_chamfer_max` (column U), whose meaning the extension lines do NOT settle -- it is now the highest-value item for a third reader.

Grip tolerance and length tolerance are folded here as independent variates. They are not: T = length - grip is a reference dimension, so the worst-case spread on `thread_region_T` (7.5692 .. 8.8392) is wider than the real part can be. Whether the standard controls length, grip, or both as the independent feature is not stated.

assembly_status.nomenclature: BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .1900" ID X .1875" LONG

gaps: A Joby detail part, not a standard -- it belongs to part-level harvesting (groundwork item 4), not the fastener library. Its part drawing is not in this repo, so the 4.63/4.76 limits are untraced.

Added 2026-08-04 (pitch_link_stack): the 4.63/4.76 limits above came from the 260729 workbook, so a from-scratch stack may not use them (SOP Step 5b: zero workbook-sourced values). pitch_link_to_pitch_plate therefore folds this bushing with a ZERO-WIDTH band at the .1875 in nominal, which makes its worst-case intervals lower bounds. The 214820-002 part drawing is the single cheapest fix.
qty 8 on 217755 = 3 tangential-link places + 5 pitch-link places; the DETAIL B balloon prefix reads 8X. That split is inferred from the two bolt counts (3X find 35, 5X find 38), not stated anywhere.

gaps: The as-drawn retention at the tan-link joint. The workbook models a plain nut and never touches castellation geometry, so nothing here is transcribed. Slot count/depth and the mating cotter-hole position are exactly what a castle-nut check needs and exactly what is missing.

Added 2026-08-04 (pitch_link_stack): MS9363-09 also retains the 5-place PITCH-LINK joint in the same view (DETAIL B, balloon prefix 8X = 3 + 5), so it now blocks two joints, not one. The bolt half of the alignment problem is CLOSED -- NAS6403 sheet 1 gives the cotter-hole position M = .174/.154 in from the point. What is still missing is entirely on the nut side: NUT HEIGHT, slot count, and slot depth (equivalently the thread-start-to-castellation spacing JPS00094 section 5.9.7 footnote (a) says varies between nuts). Promoted to the single highest-value spec-library intake item.
Same as MS9363-09, for the VPA joint.

assembly_status.nomenclature: PIN, COTTER (SPLIT), CRES, .063" DIA X .750" LONG

gaps: Cotter-hole position on the mating bolt is unknown -- it is a NAS6403 feature.

CLOSED 2026-08-04 (pitch_link_stack): NAS6403-NAS6420 Rev 4 sheet 1 gives it. M = .174/.154 in from the bolt point to the hole centreline, drill P = .080/.070 in dia, and sheet 2 note (j) 'Cotter pin hole centerline: Within .010 and normal within 2 degrees of bolt centerline'. The .063 in pin in a .070/.080 in hole is consistent. What remains is the MS9363 nut side, not this pin. JPS00094 Rev C section 5.7.6.a additionally requires cotter pins to conform to NASM24665 unless the drawing says otherwise -- worth noting that the parts list calls MS24665, the process spec calls NASM24665.
